title: Shaping timbers and polymers
needs: Make an accurate saw cut in four steps.
Choose the right saw, drill bit or abrasive for timber or polymer.
Know what each power and machine tool is used for.
Explain why CNC turning is used commercially.

doNow.q: Which hand saw cuts curved lines through thin material?

doNow.a: Wearing or scraping material away by friction.

doNow.q: Hardwoods come from which type of tree?
doNow.a: Deciduous: broad-leaved trees that lose their leaves in winter.

doNow.q: What happens to a thermoforming polymer when it is heated?
doNow.a: It softens and can be reshaped, again and again.

clues: Always use me in the direction of the grain.

chunks.label: Sawing and cutting
chunks.summary: Wasting: cutting away material you don't need from a larger piece.

items.text: Four steps for a clean, accurate cut:
steps: Mark out the cutting line, measuring from a datum point.
Clamp the material or hold it in a vice so it can't move.
Draw the saw backwards to make a nick at the start point, then use the whole blade without pressing hard.
Support the end piece as you finish so the cut stays clean. Remove rough edges.

items.text: Cuts wood along the grain (rip) or across it (cross-cut).
Shallow, accurate cuts in small pieces of wood, such as wood joints.
Curved cuts through thin material.
Fine teeth for hard materials, such as plastic pipe.
Handheld power tool with a narrow, reciprocating blade. Cuts straight lines or curves.

check.q: What is the first step before cutting?
check.a: Mark out the cutting line, measuring from a datum point.

check.q: Which saw would you use for a wood joint in a small piece of pine?

chunks.label: Shaping tools
chunks.summary: Hand and power tools that shape and smooth timber.

items.text: Bevelled blade; carves, chips and pares wood. Struck with a mallet.
Shapes and smooths wood by slicing thin shavings. Always plane with the grain.
A wheel or pad covered in abrasive paper that spins or vibrates fast to remove waste.
Handheld. Cuts a shape or profile by moving through the material.
The router follows a programmed cutting path. The material is fixed to a bed and only the router moves.

check.a: In the direction of the grain.

check.q: What moves during CNC routing: the material or the router?
check.a: Only the router. The material is fixed to the cutting bed.

chunks.label: Drilling
chunks.summary: A drill bit cuts a circular hole.

items.text: Cuts a wider recess so a screw head sits flush with, or just below, the surface.
Wide, flat blade for larger-diameter holes.
A cylindrical blade that cuts bigger holes.
Marks and starts a hole accurately before drilling or screwing.
General-purpose bit for drilling holes.

check.q: Which bit lets a screw head sit flush with the surface?
What would you use to mark a hole's position accurately before drilling?

chunks.label: Abrading
chunks.summary: Wearing or scraping material away by friction.

items.text: A coarse file with separate teeth for shaping wood. Leaves a rough surface that needs sanding.
Removes small amounts of material. Comes in many shapes and grades of coarseness.
Sandpaper, from coarse to fine. Rubbed on a surface to shape and smooth it.
Waterproof abrasive paper, used with water. Gives acrylic edges a very smooth finish.

check.q: Why does wood need sanding after using a rasp?
check.a: A rasp leaves a rough surface.

chunks.label: Machine tools
chunks.summary: Powered, fixed machines for faster, more accurate work.

items.text: Rotating abrasive paper. Sands, or strips surfaces such as old paint.
A long continuous blade running between two wheels. Very large cuts, or curves with a finer blade.
Depth stop and adjustable table: accurate holes of a set depth at 90°.

check.q: What does the depth stop on a pillar drill do?
check.a: Makes sure every hole is drilled to the same set depth.

check.q: Which machine would you use to cut a large curve in thick timber?
check.a: A band saw with a finer blade.

chunks.label: Turning
chunks.summary: Shaping material while it spins on a lathe.

items.text: Spins the work while a tool cuts, sands or shapes it all round.
Identical, accurate parts: stair spindles, chair parts, table legs.

check.q: Name two products made by commercial CNC turning.
check.a: Any two: stair spindles, chair parts, table legs, architectural columns.

check.q: Why is CNC used for turning chair legs?
check.a: Each leg is accurately sized and identical, so they fit and match.

apply.q: A furniture workshop needs to cut a very large panel of timber.
reasons: Its long continuous blade makes very large cuts
It's a hand tool, so it's more accurate

apply.q: You need to smooth the cut edge of an acrylic phone stand.
reasons: Used with water, it gives acrylic edges a very smooth finish
Its coarse teeth shape material quickly
It slices thin shavings along the grain
It strips thick surfaces such as old paint

reasons: Every leg is accurately sized and identical, so they fit and match
It leaves a rough surface that holds paint
It can only cut straight lines
It doesn't need a programmed path

oddOne.q: Which is the odd one out?

items.why: The only one for cutting wood joints.
The only hand saw that cuts curves.
The only one not used on timber: it's for hard materials such as plastic pipe.
The only one that isn't a saw: it slices shavings rather than cutting through.

order.q: Put the steps for an accurate saw cut in order.
steps: Mark out from a datum point
Draw the saw back to make a nick
Support the end piece and finish

quiz.q: A rasp leaves a smooth finish.
quiz.why: A rasp leaves a rough surface that needs sanding.

quiz.q: A pillar drill usually drills at 90°.
quiz.why: Its table and column keep the bit at 90°.

quiz.q: Wet and dry paper is used with water.
quiz.why: Its waterproof backing allows it.

quiz.q: What does 'wasting' mean?
options: Cutting away unwanted material from a larger piece
quiz.why: Sawing, drilling and abrading are all wasting.

quiz.q: After marking out, what is the next step for an accurate cut?
options: Press hard on the first stroke
quiz.why: Clamping stops the material moving.

quiz.q: Which saw cuts wood joints in small pieces of wood?
quiz.why: A tenon saw makes shallow, accurate cuts.

quiz.q: A jig saw blade moves with which motion?
quiz.why: Back and forth in a straight line.

quiz.q: In CNC routing, what moves?
quiz.why: The material is fixed to a bed and the router follows a programmed path.

quiz.q: Which bit lets a screw head sit flush?
quiz.why: It cuts a wider recess for the screw head.

quiz.q: Which tool has separate teeth and leaves wood rough?
quiz.why: A rasp shapes quickly but needs sanding after.

quiz.q: What does a pillar drill's depth stop do?
options: Drills every hole to a set depth
quiz.why: It controls how far the bit goes in.

quiz.q: Why is CNC used to turn stair spindles?
options: Every spindle is accurate and identical
It is the only way to cut timber
It leaves a rough surface for paint
quiz.why: Parts must fit and match each other.

quiz.q: A tenon saw is used for long cuts along the grain of a timber board.
quiz.why: That is a rip saw. A tenon saw makes shallow, accurate cuts in small pieces of wood.

quiz.q: A chisel is struck with a mallet to give it cutting force.
quiz.why: The mallet hits the handle so the bevelled blade cuts into the wood.

quiz.q: Which hand tool carves, chips and pares wood to shape?
quiz.why: Chisels have a bevelled blade and come in many shapes and widths.

quiz.q: Which bit is the general-purpose choice for drilling holes in timber or plastic?
quiz.why: A twist bit is the everyday bit for holes in timber or plastic.

quiz.q: What is a flat bit used for?
options: Letting a screw head sit flush
quiz.why: Its wide, flat blade cuts larger holes.

quiz.q: A band saw has a long continuous blade running between two wheels.
quiz.why: Fitting a finer blade lets it cut curves and shapes too.

quiz.q: Which machine would you use to strip old paint off a timber surface?
quiz.why: Its rotating abrasive paper can remove thick surfaces such as old paint.

quiz.q: When turning on a lathe, what spins?
options: Nothing: the tool moves round the work
quiz.why: The work spins at speed while a tool is held against it.

written.q: Describe how to make an accurate straight cut across a length of pine using a tenon saw.
points: Mark out the line, measuring from a datum point.
Clamp the pine or hold it in a vice.
Draw the saw backwards to make a starting nick.
Use the full length of the blade without pressing hard.
Support the end piece as the cut finishes.
Remove rough edges after cutting.
written.model: Mark out the cutting line, measuring from a datum point. Clamp the pine in a vice so it can't move. Draw the saw backwards to make a starting nick, then use the full length of the blade without pressing hard. Support the end piece as the cut finishes, then remove any rough edges.

written.q: A batch of beech toy parts each needs a hole drilled to the same depth. Explain why a pillar drill is a good choice.
points: It has a depth stop.
So every hole is drilled to the same set depth.
It drills accurately at 90°.
written.model: A pillar drill has a depth stop, so every hole in the batch is drilled to the same set depth.
written.note: 1 mark for a feature, 1 for why it helps. Up to 2.

written.q: A manufacturer makes 500 identical oak table legs. Explain one reason for using CNC turning rather than turning each leg by hand.
points: Each leg is accurately sized.
They are identical, so they fit and match in the final product.
written.model: CNC turning makes each leg accurately sized and identical, so all the legs fit and match in the finished tables.
written.note: 1 mark for the reason, 1 for developing it.

written.q: Compare a coping saw and a band saw for cutting curved shapes in timber.
points: Coping saw: a hand saw that cuts curves…
…but only through thin material.
Band saw: a machine with a long continuous blade running between two wheels.
A band saw cuts curves and shapes when it is fitted with a finer blade.
A band saw can also make very large cuts.
written.model: A coping saw is a hand saw that cuts curves, but only through thin material. A band saw is a machine with a long continuous blade running between two wheels. Fitted with a finer blade it cuts curves and shapes, and it can also make very large cuts.
written.note: 1 mark per point, up to 4. Full marks need a point about each saw.

written.q: A pupil needs to shape and smooth a curved edge on a pine shelf bracket. Evaluate using a rasp, a file and abrasive paper for this job.
points: A rasp is coarse, with separate teeth, so it shapes the wood.
But a rasp leaves a rough surface that needs sanding.
A file removes only small amounts of material, so it suits fine shaping.
Files come in many shapes and grades of coarseness, so a suitable one can be chosen.
Abrasive paper comes from coarse to fine, so it can shape and then smooth the surface.
Justified conclusion, e.g. shape with the rasp, then smooth with abrasive paper from coarse to fine.
written.model: A rasp is coarse and has separate teeth, so it shapes the curve in the pine well, but it leaves a rough surface that needs sanding. A file removes only small amounts of material, so it is better for fine shaping, and its many shapes and grades mean a suitable one can be chosen. Abrasive paper goes from coarse to fine, so it can finish the shaping and then smooth the surface. The best approach is to shape the curve with the rasp, then smooth it with abrasive paper, working from coarse to fine.

levels.text: Detailed, balanced points on both sides, with a justified conclusion.
Some points, mostly on one side, or a conclusion that isn't justified.

written.note: Tick the points made, then use the levels under the model answer to decide the mark.

written.q: Describe how to make a hole in a pine board so a screw head sits flush with the surface.
points: Mark and start the hole accurately with a bradawl.
Drill the hole with a twist bit.
Use a countersink bit to cut a wider recess at the top of the hole.
So the screw head sits flush with, or just below, the surface.
written.model: Mark and start the hole accurately with a bradawl, then drill it with a twist bit. Finish with a countersink bit, which cuts a wider recess at the top so the screw head sits flush with, or just below, the surface.
